name: Freeez
label: Beggars Banquet
lede: John Rocca borrowed from his grandmother to press a jazz-funk single, walked into Arthur Baker's New York office without an appointment, and came home with "I.O.U."

hero.by: John Rocca in the studio, 1979. Wikimedia Commons

eras.title: Stencils at his mother's house
eras.text: Freeez came out of London's Brit-funk scene: jazz-funk players in a basement, records bought from importers. John Rocca wanted one thing, a record of their own, and paid for it himself.

years.src: Ban Ban Ton Ton: Interview, John Rocca · Wikipedia: Freeez
years.h: A record-shop meeting near Liverpool Street
years.p: Rocca, working for a soul and jazz-funk importer, meets guitarist Jean-Paul "Bluey" Maunick, later of Incognito. Rocca joins the band rehearsing weekly in an East London basement.
years.xp:
Rocca had learned percussion from a Ghanaian musician. Wikipedia credits him with starting Freeez; in his own telling, Bluey had already assembled the group and Rocca got in by handing over a demo tape.

The core around him: Andy Stennett on keyboards, Peter Maas on bass, and Paul Morgan or Everton McCalla on drums.

q: I'd never contemplated, nor wanted fame, just to make a record.
years.src: Ban Ban Ton Ton: Interview, John Rocca · Wikipedia: Freeez · Wikipedia: John Rocca
years.h: Rocca's grandmother helps pay for "Keep in Touch"
years.p: Savings plus a loan from his gran buy an overnight West End studio session. His brother Danny designs the Pink Rhythm label, and the sleeves are stenciled at their mother's house.
years.xp: Disc Empire distributed it, it sold thousands, reached No. 49 on the UK chart, and was then licensed to Pye.

eras.title: Southern Freeez goes Top 10
eras.text: Rocca put what was left of the money into an album and kept quiet about it. Beggars Banquet picked it up, and a jazz-funk band was suddenly on Top of the Pops.

years.src: Ban Ban Ton Ton: Interview, John Rocca · Beggars Banquet: Freeez
years.h: Out of Pye, Rocca spends the rest on an album
years.p: Southern Freeez first appears on his own Pink Rhythm label. He kept the sessions secret so nobody could beat him to the sound.

years.src: Ban Ban Ton Ton: Interview, John Rocca · Wikipedia: Freeez · Beggars Banquet: Freeez
years.h: Ingrid Mansfield Allman sings "Southern Freeez" to No. 8
years.p: Rocca searched hard for the voice and spent eight hours on her vocal. The single goes silver, and the band plays Top of the Pops more than once.
years.xp: Rocca on the experience: he thought of his face "looking out of tellys all over the UK."

years.src: Beggars Banquet: Freeez · Wikipedia: Freeez · DMC World: Back to Mine with John Rocca
yt: Southern Freeez on Top of the Pops, 1981
years.p: The album climbs to No. 17. "Mariposa" became a favorite, and a Mannix disco remix came out in 2026.

eras.title: New York, no appointment
eras.text: Rocca took the band to New York to find Arthur Baker, the producer behind 'Planet Rock'. Three months later they had a UK No. 2 and a US dance No. 1, and an argument over who wrote it.

years.cap: Andy Stennett, Arthur Baker, John Rocca and Peter Maas in New York, 1982
years.src: Ban Ban Ton Ton: Interview, John Rocca
years.h: Rocca walks into Arthur Baker's office uninvited
years.p: Rocca and three bandmates show up in New York without an appointment. Baker already owns a copy of Southern Freeez, and they stay three months.

years.src: Wikipedia: I.O.U. (Freeez song) · Wikipedia: Freeez · Wikipedia: John Rocca · Beggars Banquet: Freeez
years.h: "I.O.U." hits No. 2 in Britain and tops the US dance chart
years.p: Baker wrote and produced it at Unique Studios; Jellybean Benitez remixed it. The video has kids on BMX bikes and skateboards acting out New York hip-hop.
years.xp:
It held No. 1 on Billboard's dance chart for two weeks, made No. 3 in Australia and No. 13 on the US R&B chart, went gold in the UK and was the 20th best-selling single of 1983 there. Wikipedia calls it one of the first records to use digital sampling.

It has been sampled since by [[Jamie xx|d1515727-4a93-4c0d-88cb-d7a9fce01879]], Brandy, Coolio and Madlib, among others.

years.cap: John Rocca and Peter Maas, c. 1983
years.src: Ban Ban Ton Ton: Interview, John Rocca · Discogs: Freeez featuring John Rocca, IOU · Wikipedia: Freeez
yt: I.O.U. on Top of the Pops, 1983
years.h: Rocca says he wrote the words to "I.O.U." without credit
years.p: Wikipedia credits the lyrics to Rocca; Discogs lists Baker and John Robie as writers. Rocca says he let it go so he could finish and go home.
years.xp: Rocca to Ban Ban Ton Ton: "By then it made sense to get things finished, so I could go back to England."

years.h: Gonna Get You and "Pop Goes My Love"
years.p: The album reaches No. 46. "Pop Goes My Love" and its flip "Scratch Goes My Dub" go top five on the US dance chart and No. 26 in the UK.

eras.title: Freeez without Rocca
eras.text: Rocca went solo and kept hitting No. 1 on the American dance charts. Peter Maas kept the name and took a new Freeez to Abbey Road.

years.p: The breakdance film puts the song in front of a new crowd.

years.h: Peter Maas keeps the name; Rocca goes solo
years.p: Louis Smith and songwriter-guitarist Billy Crichton join Maas. Rocca's "I Want It to Be Real" tops the US dance chart the same year.

years.h: Idle Vice is cut in the Beatles' room at Abbey Road
years.p: Studio 2. "That Beats My Patience" is the first single. Rocca and Stennett, meanwhile, record as Pictures and Pink Rhythm.

eras.title: Remixes, Midi Rain and a degree
eras.text: The hits kept coming back in new mixes. Rocca had one more dance No. 1 in him, then walked away from music for computers.

years.p: The Citybeat remix gets to No. 23 in the UK; a "Southern Freeez" remix reaches No. 63.

years.src: Wikipedia: John Rocca · Ban Ban Ton Ton: Interview, John Rocca · Wikipedia: Freeez
years.h: Rocca's last record as Midi Rain is a No. 1, so he stops
years.p: "Shine" tops the US dance chart, and he retires late that year. A first-class degree from Middlesex University follows in 1995, then a telecom startup.
years.xp:
Rocca: "my last recorded track was a #1, so I couldn't really have planned that better." He co-founded Intec Telecom Systems in 1997, and later settled in Kuala Lumpur.

The same year, Maas and Paul Morgan rehearsed a new band, the Dazzling Urbanites, in Muswell Hill; Wikipedia says it didn't take off.

years.h: Southern Freeez returns as a double CD
years.p: Twelve-inch versions, remixes and demos, with new notes from Rocca and Maas; Gonna Get You gets the same treatment.
